title: Twelve, seven, five
hookLine: Twelver Shia follow twelve Imams, Isma'ilis a different line after Ja'far, Zaydis another after Ali Zayn al-Abidin

cards: A family tree has a way of forking. Two brothers, two inheritances, two sets of cousins who each tell the story from their own branch. The Shia line of Imams forked too, more than once, and the forks have names.
Outsiders sometimes call them by numbers: Twelvers, Seveners, Fivers. Those nicknames are rough, and the communities have their own names for themselves.
But the numbers open a question Shia Muslims had to answer more than once: when an Imam dies, which son carries the line?

teach.h: THE FIRST FORK: AFTER ZAYN AL-ABIDIN.
teach.b: All three tell their story back through Ali and Fatima, Hasan and Husayn. The first fork comes after Husayn's son Ali Zayn al-Abidin, al-Sajjad. One of his sons, Zayd, rose up in Kufa against the Umayyads and was killed.
Those who held that an Imam is any descendant of Hasan or Husayn who stands up openly against injustice followed Zayd's example.
They are the Zaydis, and because Zayd comes fifth when the line is counted from Ali, outsiders call them Fivers. Zaydi communities live in Yemen today.
Others held that the line had already passed from Zayn al-Abidin to Zayd's brother, Muhammad al-Baqir, and then to Ja'far al-Sadiq. The second fork comes after Ja'far.
Some held that the line passed through his son Isma'il and Isma'il's son. They are the Isma'ilis, sometimes called Seveners.
Isma'ili communities today have their own branches, and some follow a living Imam, present in the world now.

teach.h: MUSA, TO THE TWELFTH: THE TWELVERS.
teach.b: Others followed Ja'far's son Musa, called al-Kazim, the one who holds back his anger, and the line went on, father to son, to a twelfth Imam.

These are the Twelvers, the Ithna Ashariyya, the Shia of Iran, Iraq, Lebanon and beyond, whose law, as yesterday said, is called Ja'fari. Each line holds that it kept faith with the Prophet's family, peace be upon him.
Each has its own scholars, its own prayers, its own sense of what an Imam is. None of them is a footnote to another.

how: Twelver, Isma'ili and Zaydi Shia Muslims each honor their own line of Imams descended from Ali and Fatima; some Isma'ili communities follow a living Imam today.

games.q: you're a follower of Ja'far al-Sadiq when he dies. whose line do you follow next?
games.why: Isma'ilis followed the line through Isma'il; Twelvers followed Musa al-Kazim. both lines continue today.

practice: Say the three names slowly in your head: Zaydi, Isma'ili, Ithna Ashari, Twelver. Pick one you hadn't heard before and hold it the way you'd hold a new neighbor's name, wanting to get it right.
Wonder what you'd like to know about the people who carry it, and keep the question, not an answer.

wordCard.voice: Twelve. The Twelver Shia line of Imams, from Ali to the twelfth, beside the Isma'ili and Zaydi lines that forked from it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one who stands in front; for Shia Muslims, a leader from the Prophet's family.

carryVoice: Your line: three lines of imams. Shia Muslims are more than one community. Rest well.
